message.content:
当前基线已持久化请求状态事件和链哈希，HTTP 层已有受理、状态、执行日志、墓碑和对账入口，但客户端还不能直接从 HTTP 契约取得请求级完整性结论。我这次只增加 GET /requests/{request_id}/evidence 只读入口，查询删除请求的当前状态记录与审计链是否自洽，不含前端工作，不改变现有入口的响应和错误口径。

请求沿用现有 GET 子资源的租户定位与 request:read 鉴权，可由 X-Tenant-Id 头或 tenant_id 查询参数指定租户。成功响应使用 application/json，正文为一行紧凑 UTF-8 JSON 加一个换行，字段固定为 request_id、status、event_count、chain_hash、verified。request_id 是被查询请求，status 和 event_count 是同一数据库快照中的当前状态与状态事件数，chain_hash 是该快照持久化的 64 位小写十六进制链头；verified 仅在同一快照逐事件重算哈希、序号从 0 连续、末事件状态等于当前状态、末链哈希等于请求记录绑定链头时为 true，否则为 false。五个字段必须来自同一个已提交快照，状态推进或并发写入不得让一次响应混合两个事务的结果。

请求号格式非法、不存在或属于其他租户时返回 404 not_found，不区分缺失与越权；租户缺失或非法返回 400 invalid_request，鉴权失败保持现有 401 unauthorized 与 403 forbidden 的顺序和结果。请求记录、事件和链头可读时，即使事件被删除、改写、插入、重排或与请求重新绑定，也返回 200 且 verified 为 false；持久化链头若不是合法 SHA-256 文本，chain_hash 返回 null 且 verified 为 false。数据库不可达、读写故障或快照无法完整读取返回 503 storage_unavailable，错误正文只有 error 字段，不泄露 SQL、路径、租户、主体、范围内容或令牌。该 GET 不得创建或修改请求、状态事件、执行尝试、墓碑、回执、策略目录或审计锚点，并保持现有全部公开入口的既有行为与兼容结果。

addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`; (5) `claude plugin eval` (writing and running plugin eval suites, its JSON/report, sandbox, CI, early-access enablement) and the `/skill-doctor` report. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Glob, Grep, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ArtifactComments, ArtifactData, ArtifactCheck, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ArtifactComments, ArtifactData, ArtifactCheck, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

1	"""HTTP layer for deletion-request acceptance, lookup, observation and
2	single-request reconciliation.
3	
4	The service exposes eight business endpoints:
5	
6	* ``POST /requests`` -- accept a deletion request for a tenant. The JSON
7	  body must carry non-empty ``tenant_id``, ``subject_id`` and
8	  ``idempotency_key`` strings plus a non-empty ``scopes`` array of
9	  distinct non-empty strings.
10	* ``GET /requests`` -- the tenant-scoped, paginated listing of accepted
11	  requests. The tenant follows the existing ``X-Tenant-Id``/query rule;
12	  the optional ``status`` (comma-separated distinct lifecycle statuses),
13	  ``created_from`` (inclusive) and ``created_to`` (exclusive) RFC3339 UTC
14	  bounds, ``cursor`` and ``limit`` (1..1000, default 100) query
15	  parameters filter and page the result. The single-line JSON body
16	  carries exactly ``items`` and ``next_cursor``; each item carries
17	  exactly ``request_id``, ``status`` and ``created_at`` in ascending
18	  acceptance order, and ``next_cursor`` is the opaque continuation value
19	  or ``null`` at the end of the listing. Any other query parameter, a
20	  duplicated ``status`` value or a malformed filter answers 400.
21	* ``GET /requests/{request_id}`` -- return the accepted request's
22	  receipt, scoped to the tenant identified by the ``X-Tenant-Id`` header
23	  (or a ``tenant_id`` query parameter). The receipt is the record frozen
24	  at acceptance time and always reports ``accepted``; it never changes
25	  when the request's status subsequently advances.
26	* ``GET /requests/{request_id}/status`` -- read-only observation of the
27	  request's current state. The single-line JSON body carries exactly
28	  ``request_id``, ``status`` and ``created_at`` in that order; ``status``
29	  is the latest persisted state while ``created_at`` stays the original
30	  acceptance time.
31	* ``GET /requests/{request_id}/execution-log`` -- read-only observation
32	  of the request's execution attempts. The single-line JSON body carries
33	  exactly ``request_id`` and ``attempts``; attempts are ordered by
34	  ``attempt_number`` starting at 1 and each entry carries exactly
35	  ``attempt_number``, ``claimed_at``, ``lease_expires_at``, ``result``
36	  and ``completed_at``. An unfinished attempt has ``null`` ``result`` and
37	  ``completed_at``; a finished attempt carries its stored ``completed``
38	  or ``failed`` result and completion time.
39	* ``GET /requests/{request_id}/tombstones`` -- read-only, paginated
40	  publication of the tenant's deletion proofs for one request. The
41	  tenant follows the existing ``X-Tenant-Id``/query rule; the only
42	  query parameters are ``cursor`` and ``limit`` (1..1000, default 100).
43	  The single-line JSON body carries exactly ``request_id``,
44	  ``tombstones``, ``recorded_at``, ``evidence_digest`` and
45	  ``next_cursor`` in that order. ``tombstones`` holds only this page's
46	  entries in ascending normalized-scope Unicode code point order then
47	  ascending ``adapter_id``; each entry carries exactly ``adapter_id``,
48	  ``scope``, ``operation_id``, ``outcome`` (``deleted`` or ``absent``),
49	  ``proof_digest`` (64 lowercase hex characters) and ``recorded_at``.
50	  The top-level ``recorded_at`` and ``evidence_digest`` always describe
51	  the whole ledger (both ``null`` when it is empty), never just the
52	  page; ``next_cursor`` resumes strictly after this page's last entry
53	  while the ledger holds a following item and is ``null`` at the end.
54	  An unknown or duplicated query parameter, an invalid ``limit`` or an
55	  empty, malformed, foreign or stale ``cursor`` answers 400; an
56	  invalid, unknown or cross-tenant request id answers 404; a storage
57	  fault or a corrupt ledger answers 503 and never a partial page or a
58	  pseudo digest. The read never advances state, never creates an
59	  attempt or a tombstone and never changes the audit chain.
60	* ``GET /policy-catalog/versions`` -- read-only publication of the
61	  tenant's policy-catalog version history, without any subject detail.
62	  The tenant follows the existing ``X-Tenant-Id``/query rule; the query
63	  string accepts no parameter other than ``tenant_id`` -- a duplicated
64	  key, an unknown parameter or an empty or malformed tenant answers 400.
65	  The body is the verbatim single-line compact UTF-8 JSON text (with its
66	  single trailing newline) produced by
67	  :meth:`RequestStore.audit_policy_catalog`: exactly ``versions`` at the
68	  top level, versions in ascending order, each carrying exactly
69	  ``version``, ``effective_at``, ``rule_count``, ``exception_count`` and
70	  ``status`` -- never a policy id, selector, reason, subject or any raw
71	  catalog content. The read never creates or advances a catalog version,
72	  request, attempt, tombstone, receipt or audit record, so repeated
73	  reads and reads after a restart return the same snapshot. A tenant
74	  without publications answers 200 with an empty ``versions`` array; a
75	  corrupt catalog or any storage failure answers 503 and never a
76	  partial history or a fabricated summary.
77	* ``POST /requests/{request_id}/reconcile`` -- reconcile exactly one
78	  request's execution record against its persisted state by calling the
79	  storage layer's :meth:`RequestStore.reconcile_execution`. The endpoint
80	  takes no business parameters: a missing ``Content-Length`` or a length
81	  of zero means there is no body; any other body answers 400. On success
82	  it answers 200 with the same single-line JSON shape as the status
83	  read -- exactly ``request_id``, ``status`` and ``created_at`` --
84	  rendering the current record after reconciliation. Repeating the call
85	  never changes a stable terminal state, historical attempts or existing
86	  timestamps; concurrent calls leave the unique outcome to the store's
87	  atomic commit. No subject, scope, idempotency key, worker, lease
88	  credential or attempt detail is ever exposed.
89	
90	The observation endpoints never advance state, create an attempt or
91	write any bookkeeping; they only read persisted rows, so their answers
92	match the persisted records after a restart. They never expose a lease
93	credential, worker identity, subject, scope or any other request field.
94	Only the single-request reconcile endpoint may converge execution state,
95	through the storage layer's existing atomic semantics; no batch
96	reconciliation is exposed over HTTP.
97	
98	Status advancement (:meth:`RequestStore.transition`), the execution
99	orchestration (:meth:`RequestStore.claim_next`,
100	:meth:`RequestStore.finish_claim`, :meth:`RequestStore.renew_lease`,
101	:meth:`RequestStore.transfer_claim`,
102	:meth:`RequestStore.reconcile_batch`,
103	:meth:`RequestStore.migrate_execution_leases`) and the deletion receipts
104	(:meth:`RequestStore.generate_receipt`,
105	:meth:`RequestStore.verify_receipt`,
106	:meth:`RequestStore.rotate_receipt_key`) and the anchor capability
107	(:meth:`RequestStore.verify_chain`,
108	:meth:`RequestStore.diagnose_chain`,
109	:meth:`RequestStore.rotate_anchor_key`) and the read-only batched
110	audit inspection (:meth:`RequestStore.audit_inspection` and
111	:meth:`RequestStore.audit_inspection_summary`) exist only on
112	the storage layer and are deliberately not exposed over HTTP: over HTTP
113	the service opens request acceptance, the acceptance-receipt lookup, the
114	read-only tenant-scoped listing, the three read-only observation reads,
115	the single-request execution reconciliation and the read-only
116	policy-catalog version history described above. The
117	current-status lookup (:meth:`RequestStore.get_status`), the
118	tenant-scoped listing (:meth:`RequestStore.list_requests`), the
119	execution log (:meth:`RequestStore.get_execution_log`), the tombstone
120	page read (:meth:`RequestStore.page_deletion_tombstones`), the
121	single-request reconciliation
122	(:meth:`RequestStore.reconcile_execution`) and the catalog version
123	history (:meth:`RequestStore.audit_policy_catalog`) back their HTTP
124	endpoints but remain storage-layer methods as well.
125	
126	Success responses are a single line of JSON followed by a trailing
127	newline. Acceptance, receipt lookup, the status read and a successful
128	reconcile render exactly ``request_id``, ``status`` and ``created_at``
129	(in that order); the same idempotent request and every lookup return
130	byte-identical bodies. The execution-log read renders exactly
131	``request_id`` and ``attempts``. The
132	listing read renders exactly ``items`` and ``next_cursor``, each item
133	rendering exactly ``request_id``, ``status`` and ``created_at``. The
134	tombstone page read renders exactly ``request_id``, ``tombstones``,
135	``recorded_at``, ``evidence_digest`` and ``next_cursor``, each
136	tombstone rendering exactly ``adapter_id``, ``scope``, ``operation_id``,
137	``outcome``, ``proof_digest`` and ``recorded_at``. The policy-catalog
138	history read renders exactly ``versions``, each version rendering
139	exactly ``version``, ``effective_at``, ``rule_count``,
140	``exception_count`` and ``status``.
141	Error responses are single-line JSON objects with exactly one key,
142	``error``, holding a stable error code:
143	
144	``invalid_request`` (400), ``unauthorized`` (401), ``forbidden``
145	(403), ``idempotency_conflict`` (409), ``not_found`` (404),
146	``method_not_allowed`` (405) and ``storage_unavailable`` (503).
147	
148	Optional token authentication and role-based access control can be
149	enabled by passing an auth configuration (see :func:`load_auth_config`)
150	to :func:`build_server` / :func:`make_handler`. Without it the service
151	keeps the unauthenticated contract described above. When enabled every
152	matched business request must present ``Authorization: Bearer <token>``
153	for a configured principal: a missing/malformed/unknown token answers
154	``401 unauthorized`` and a principal lacking the role required by the
155	endpoint, or acting on a tenant other than its own ``tenant_id``,
156	answers ``403 forbidden``. ``POST /requests`` requires
157	``request:submit`` and the target tenant is the body's ``tenant_id``;
158	each of the five GET endpoints requires ``request:read`` and the target
159	tenant follows the existing ``X-Tenant-Id``/query rule; the
160	single-request reconciliation ``POST /requests/{request_id}/reconcile``
161	requires ``request:reconcile`` and its target tenant follows the same
162	existing ``X-Tenant-Id``/query rule; the policy-catalog history
163	``GET /policy-catalog/versions`` requires ``policy:read`` and its
164	target tenant follows the same existing ``X-Tenant-Id``/query rule.
165	The configuration keeps accepting the ``request:submit``,
166	``request:read`` and ``request:reconcile`` roles alone: a principal
167	without ``policy:read`` simply cannot use the catalog endpoint, and an
168	existing configuration without it never fails to load. Authentication runs after
169	path/method routing (unknown paths stay 404, unsupported methods stay
170	405) but before payload validation and any storage access.
171	Tokens, roles and the configuration never enter a response, a raised
172	exception message, a log record, the database or any stored artifact.
173	
174	No subject, scope, idempotency key, lease credential, worker identity,
175	database error text, SQL statement or filesystem path is ever placed in
176	a response, a log record or a raised exception message.
177	"""
178	
179	from __future__ import annotations
180	
181	import json
182	import logging
183	import re
184	import sqlite3
185	import threading
186	from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, ThreadingHTTPServer
187	from urllib.parse import parse_qs, urlsplit
188	
189	from .requests import IdempotencyConflict, RequestNotFound, RequestStore
190	
191	__all__ = [
192	    "build_server",
193	    "make_handler",
194	    "DeferredRequestStore",
195	    "AuthConfig",
196	    "AuthConfigError",
197	    "load_auth_config",
198	]
199	
200	_log = logging.getLogger(__name__)
201	
202	_COLLECTION_PATH = "/requests"
203	_ITEM_PATH_PREFIX = "/requests/"
204	_POLICY_CATALOG_VERSIONS_PATH = "/policy-catalog/versions"
205	_STATUS_RESOURCE = "status"
206	_EXECUTION_LOG_RESOURCE = "execution-log"
207	_TOMBSTONES_RESOURCE = "tombstones"
208	_RECONCILE_RESOURCE = "reconcile"
209	_TENANT_HEADER = "X-Tenant-Id"
210	_AUTHORIZATION_HEADER = "Authorization"
211	_BEARER_PREFIX = "Bearer "
212	
213	# Reject oversized request bodies before they reach the database layer.
214	_MAX_BODY_BYTES = 1 << 20  # 1 MiB
215	
216	_ROLE_SUBMIT = "request:submit"
217	_ROLE_READ = "request:read"
218	_ROLE_RECONCILE = "request:reconcile"
219	_ROLE_POLICY_READ = "policy:read"
220	_ALLOWED_ROLES = frozenset(
221	    {_ROLE_SUBMIT, _ROLE_READ, _ROLE_RECONCILE, _ROLE_POLICY_READ}
222	)
223	
224	# Terminal attempt results, mirrored from the execution state machine so a
225	# corrupt or substituted store can never serialise another value.
226	_TERMINAL_RESULTS = frozenset({"completed", "failed"})

290	class AuthConfig:
291	    """Parsed, immutable bearer-token principals for RBAC.
292	
293	    Principals map a non-empty bearer token to their tenant id and a set
294	    of roles. Tokens and roles are kept in process memory only and are
295	    never logged or persisted by this module.
296	    """
297	
298	    def __init__(self, principals: list[dict]):
299	        # ``principals`` has already passed :func:`load_auth_config`; copy
300	        # into an immutable token -> (tenant_id, frozenset(roles)) map.
301	        by_token: dict[str, tuple[str, frozenset[str]]] = {}
302	        for principal in principals:
303	            by_token[principal["token"]] = (
304	                principal["tenant_id"],
305	                frozenset(principal["roles"]),
306	            )
307	        self._by_token = by_token
308	
309	    def authenticate(self, token: str) -> tuple[str, frozenset[str]] | None:
310	        """Return ``(tenant_id, roles)`` for *token*, or ``None`` if unknown."""
311	        return self._by_token.get(token)

314	def load_auth_config(path: str) -> AuthConfig:
315	    """Read and validate the auth configuration file once, at startup.
316	
317	    The file must be a UTF-8 JSON object with a ``principals`` array;
318	    each principal is an object carrying non-empty ``token`` and
319	    ``tenant_id`` strings plus a non-empty ``roles`` array of distinct
320	    values drawn from ``request:submit``, ``request:read``,
321	    ``request:reconcile`` and ``policy:read``. Tokens must be unique across principals. Any
322	    deviation -- including an unreadable or non-UTF-8 file, malformed
323	    JSON, a missing ``principals`` key or a principal missing/typing-wrong
324	    one of the required keys -- raises :class:`AuthConfigError` so the
325	    caller can refuse to bind.
326	    """
327	    # Suppress exception chaining ("from None"): the underlying OSError
328	    # carries the filesystem path and a decode/JSON error may quote file
329	    # content, neither of which may reach a raised exception message.
330	    try:
331	        with open(path, "rb") as handle:
332	            raw = handle.read()
333	    except OSError:
334	        raise AuthConfigError("auth_config_invalid") from None
335	    try:
336	        parsed = json.loads(raw.decode("utf-8"))
337	    except (UnicodeDecodeError, ValueError):
338	        raise AuthConfigError("auth_config_invalid") from None
339	
340	    principals = _validate_auth_config(parsed)
341	    return AuthConfig(principals)
342	
343	
344	def _validate_auth_config(parsed: object) -> list[dict]:
345	    if not isinstance(parsed, dict) or "principals" not in parsed:
346	        raise AuthConfigError("auth_config_invalid")
347	    raw_principals = parsed["principals"]
348	    if not isinstance(raw_principals, list):
349	        raise AuthConfigError("auth_config_invalid")
350	
351	    principals: list[dict] = []
352	    seen_tokens: set[str] = set()
353	    for entry in raw_principals:
354	        # Only the three specified keys are validated; their presence,
355	        # types and value domains are mandatory.
356	        if not isinstance(entry, dict) or not {
357	            "token",
358	            "tenant_id",
359	            "roles",
360	        } <= set(entry):
361	            raise AuthConfigError("auth_config_invalid")
362	        token = entry["token"]
363	        tenant_id = entry["tenant_id"]
364	        roles = entry["roles"]
365	        if not isinstance(token, str) or not token:
366	            raise AuthConfigError("auth_config_invalid")
367	        if not isinstance(tenant_id, str) or not tenant_id:
368	            raise AuthConfigError("auth_config_invalid")
369	        if not isinstance(roles, list) or not roles:
370	            raise AuthConfigError("auth_config_invalid")
371	        if not all(isinstance(role, str) for role in roles):
372	            raise AuthConfigError("auth_config_invalid")
373	        if len(set(roles)) != len(roles) or not set(roles) <= _ALLOWED_ROLES:
374	            raise AuthConfigError("auth_config_invalid")
375	        if token in seen_tokens:
376	            raise AuthConfigError("auth_config_invalid")
377	        seen_tokens.add(token)
378	        principals.append(
379	            {"token": token, "tenant_id": tenant_id, "roles": roles}
380	        )
381	    return principals

384	class DeferredRequestStore:
385	    """Lazily (re)initialising :class:`RequestStore` wrapper.
386	
387	    Opening the store and creating the required tables is attempted once
388	    at construction (service startup); if the database cannot be created
389	    -- an unwritable path, a corrupt file, an I/O error -- startup still
390	    succeeds and every business call retries initialization, failing the
391	    single request with the stable ``storage_unavailable`` outcome. This
392	    keeps "database cannot be created" indistinguishable from "database
393	    became unusable": both answer HTTP 503 instead of taking the whole
394	    service down, and a storage path repaired at runtime heals on the
395	    next request without a restart.
396	    """
397	
398	    def __init__(self, db_path: str):
399	        self._db_path = db_path
400	        self._lock = threading.Lock()
401	        self._store: RequestStore | None = None
402	        try:
403	            self._store = RequestStore(db_path)
404	        except (OSError, sqlite3.Error, RuntimeError):
405	            _log.warning("storage unavailable at startup")
406	
407	    def _ready(self) -> RequestStore:
408	        if self._store is not None:
409	            return self._store
410	        with self._lock:
411	            if self._store is None:
412	                try:
413	                    self._store = RequestStore(self._db_path)
414	                except (OSError, sqlite3.Error, RuntimeError):
415	                    raise _StorageUnavailable
416	            return self._store
417

419	        return self._ready().submit(tenant_id, subject_id, scopes, idempotency_key)

532	    """Validate a request id as a UUID and return its canonical text."""
533	    if not _UUID_RE.match(value):

540	def build_server(
541	    store,
542	    host: str = "127.0.0.1",
543	    port: int = 8080,
544	    auth: AuthConfig | None = None,
545	) -> ThreadingHTTPServer:
546	    """Build (but do not start) the threaded HTTP server bound to *host*:*port*.
547	
548	    With *auth* ``None`` (the default) the server keeps its
549	    unauthenticated contract; pass a loaded :class:`AuthConfig` to
550	    require bearer-token authentication and RBAC on the business
551	    endpoints.
552	    """
553	    handler = make_handler(store, auth)
554	    server = ThreadingHTTPServer((host, port), handler)
555	    # Worker threads must not keep the process alive on shutdown.
556	    server.daemon_threads = True
557	    return server

560	def make_handler(
561	    store: RequestStore,
562	    auth: AuthConfig | None = None,
563	) -> type[BaseHTTPRequestHandler]:
564	    """Build a handler class closed over *store* and optional *auth*."""
565	
566	    class _DeletionRequestHandler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
567	        protocol_version = "HTTP/1.1"
568	        # Do not advertise the runtime version.
569	        server_version = "forgetting-evidence/0.1"
570	        sys_version = ""
571	
572	        def version_string(self) -> str:  # type: ignore[override]
573	            # BaseHTTPRequestHandler joins server/sys versions with a
574	            # space; with an empty sys version that leaves a trailing
575	            # space, so render the fixed token verbatim.
576	            return self.server_version
577	
578	        # -- routing ---------------------------------------------------
579	
580	        def _route(self) -> tuple[str | None, str | None]:
581	            path = urlsplit(self.path).path
582	            if path == _COLLECTION_PATH:
583	                return "collection", None
584	            if path == _POLICY_CATALOG_VERSIONS_PATH:
585	                return "policy_catalog_versions", None
586	            if path.startswith(_ITEM_PATH_PREFIX):
587	                segment = path[len(_ITEM_PATH_PREFIX) :]
588	                # Empty or nested segments do not name a request.
589	                if segment and "/" not in segment:
590	                    return "item", segment
591	                # The three read-only observability sub-resources live
592	                # under a request id: /requests/{id}/status,
593	                # /requests/{id}/execution-log and
594	                # /requests/{id}/tombstones, alongside the single
595	                # reconciliation action /requests/{id}/reconcile. Deeper
596	                # nesting or any other suffix stays an unknown path (404).
597	                if "/" in segment:
598	                    item_id, suffix = segment.split("/", 1)
599	                    if item_id and "/" not in suffix:
600	                        if suffix == _STATUS_RESOURCE:
601	                            return "status", item_id
602	                        if suffix == _EXECUTION_LOG_RESOURCE:
603	                            return "execution_log", item_id
604	                        if suffix == _TOMBSTONES_RESOURCE:
605	                            return "tombstones", item_id
606	                        if suffix == _RECONCILE_RESOURCE:
607	                            return "reconcile", item_id
608	            return None, None
609	
610	        # -- method entry points --------------------------------------
611	
612	        def do_POST(self) -> None:  # noqa: N802 - http.server naming
613	            self._guard(self._handle_post)
614	
615	        def do_GET(self) -> None:  # noqa: N802 - http.server naming
616	            self._guard(self._handle_get)
617	
618	        def do_HEAD(self) -> None:  # noqa: N802 - http.server naming
619	            # HEAD receives the same 405/404 routing as other unsupported
620	            # verbs, with headers but no body.
621	            self._guard(lambda: self._handle_unsupported_method(headless=True))
622	
623	        def do_PUT(self) -> None:  # noqa: N802 - http.server naming
624	            self._guard(self._handle_unsupported_method)
625	
626	        def do_DELETE(self) -> None:  # noqa: N802 - http.server naming
627	            self._guard(self._handle_unsupported_method)
628	
629	        def do_PATCH(self) -> None:  # noqa: N802 - http.server naming
630	            self._guard(self._handle_unsupported_method)
631	
632	        def do_OPTIONS(self) -> None:  # noqa: N802 - http.server naming
633	            self._guard(self._handle_unsupported_method)
634	
635	        def handle_expect_100(self) -> bool:  # type: ignore[override]
636	            # Honour "Expect: 100-continue" so clients (e.g. curl with a
637	            # large body) send the payload instead of waiting for a
638	            # 100-continue that never arrives.
639	            return True
640	
641	        def _guard(self, handler) -> None:
642	            try:
643	                handler()
644	            except _BadRequest:
645	                self._safe_error(400, _INVALID_REQUEST)
646	            except Exception:
647	                # A defect in request handling must surface as the
648	                # stable storage code only; never let http.server print a
649	                # traceback (which could quote SQL or paths) to stderr.
650	                _log.warning("request failed: %s", _STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE)
651	                self._safe_error(503, _STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE)
652	
653	        def _handle_unsupported_method(self, headless: bool = False) -> None:
654	            kind, _ = self._route()
655	            if kind is None:
656	                self._reply_error(404, _NOT_FOUND, headless=headless)
657	            else:
658	                # The collection accepts POST (acceptance) and GET (the
659	                # tenant-scoped listing); the item and the read-only
660	                # sub-resources are GET-only; the reconcile action is
661	                # POST-only.
662	                if kind == "collection":
663	                    allowed = "GET, POST"
664	                elif kind == "reconcile":
665	                    allowed = "POST"
666	                else:
667	                    allowed = "GET"
668	                self._reply_error(
669	                    405, _METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED, allowed=allowed, headless=headless
670	                )

672	        # -- authentication / authorization ----------------------------
673	
674	        def _authorize(self, required_role: str) -> tuple[str, frozenset[str]] | None:
675	            """Authenticate the bearer token and check *required_role*.
676	
677	            Returns the principal's ``(tenant_id, roles)`` on success.
678	            Replies ``401 unauthorized`` for a missing, malformed or
679	            unknown credential and ``403 forbidden`` when the role is
680	            absent; returns ``None`` in either case. No token material is
681	            ever logged or quoted in the response.
682	            """
683	            if auth is None:
684	                # Unauthenticated deployment: no principal and no gate.
685	                return ("", frozenset())
686	            header = self.headers.get(_AUTHORIZATION_HEADER)
687	            if header is None or not header.startswith(_BEARER_PREFIX):
688	                self._auth_rejected(401, _UNAUTHORIZED)
689	                return None
690	            token = header[len(_BEARER_PREFIX) :]
691	            if not token:
692	                self._auth_rejected(401, _UNAUTHORIZED)
693	                return None
694	            principal = auth.authenticate(token)
695	            if principal is None:
696	                self._auth_rejected(401, _UNAUTHORIZED)
697	                return None
698	            tenant_id, roles = principal
699	            if required_role not in roles:
700	                self._auth_rejected(403, _FORBIDDEN)
701	                return None
702	            return tenant_id, roles
703	
704	        def _auth_rejected(self, status: int, code: str) -> None:
705	            # A rejected POST has not consumed its request body, so the
706	            # connection cannot serve another pipelined request; close it
707	            # after the error to keep keep-alive framing intact.
708	            if self.command == "POST":
709	                self.close_connection = True
710	            self._reply_error(status, code)
711	
712	        def _tenant_allowed(
713	            self, principal_tenant: str, target_tenant: str
714	        ) -> bool:
715	            if auth is None:
716	                return True
717	            if target_tenant != principal_tenant:
718	                self._reply_error(403, _FORBIDDEN)
719	                return False
720	            return True
721	
722	        def _handle_post(self) -> None:
723	            kind, segment = self._route()
724	            if kind is None:
725	                self._reply_error(404, _NOT_FOUND)
726	                return
727	            if kind == "reconcile":
728	                assert segment is not None
729	                self._serve_reconcile(segment)
730	                return
731	            if kind != "collection":
732	                self._reply_error(405, _METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED, allowed="GET")
733	                return
734	            # Authentication precedes payload validation and storage.
735	            principal = self._authorize(_ROLE_SUBMIT)
736	            if principal is None:
737	                return
738	            payload = self._read_json_object()
739	            tenant_id = _require_string(payload, "tenant_id")
740	            # The body's tenant is the authorization target; a principal
741	            # may only submit for its own tenant.
742	            if not self._tenant_allowed(principal[0], tenant_id):
743	                return
744	            subject_id = _require_string(payload, "subject_id")
745	            idempotency_key = _require_string(payload, "idempotency_key")
746	            scopes = _require_scopes(payload)
747	            try:
748	                receipt = store.submit(
749	                    tenant_id, subject_id, scopes, idempotency_key
750	                )
751	            except ValueError:
752	                # Defence in depth: the HTTP validation above is
753	                # authoritative, but a rejected store call writes nothing
754	                # and maps to the same client error.
755	                self._reply_error(400, _INVALID_REQUEST)
756	                return
757	            except IdempotencyConflict:
758	                self._reply_error(409, _IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT)
759	                return
760	            except _StorageUnavailable:
761	                _log.warning("request rejected: %s", _STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE)
762	                self._reply_error(503, _STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE)
763	                return
764	            except (sqlite3.Error, RuntimeError, OSError):
765	                # The store deliberately raises fixed-text RuntimeErrors;
766	                # sqlite/OSError text (locks, malformed images, paths)
767	                # must never reach the client.
768	                _log.warning("request rejected: %s", _STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE)
769	                self._reply_error(503, _STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE)
770	                return
771	            self._reply_receipt(200, receipt)
772	
773	        def _handle_get(self) -> None:
774	            kind, segment = self._route()
775	            if kind is None:
776	                self._reply_error(404, _NOT_FOUND)
777	                return
778	            if kind == "collection":
779	                # The tenant-scoped, paginated listing of accepted
780	                # requests; read-only like the item observations.
781	                self._serve_list()
782	                return
783	            if kind == "policy_catalog_versions":

"""HTTP layer for deletion-request acceptance, lookup, observation and
single-request reconciliation.

The service exposes eight business endpoints:

* ``POST /requests`` -- accept a deletion request for a tenant. The JSON
  body must carry non-empty ``tenant_id``, ``subject_id`` and
  ``idempotency_key`` strings plus a non-empty ``scopes`` array of
  distinct non-empty strings.
* ``GET /requests`` -- the tenant-scoped, paginated listing of accepted
  requests. The tenant follows the existing ``X-Tenant-Id``/query rule;
  the optional ``status`` (comma-separated distinct lifecycle statuses),
  ``created_from`` (inclusive) and ``created_to`` (exclusive) RFC3339 UTC
  bounds, ``cursor`` and ``limit`` (1..1000, default 100) query
  parameters filter and page the result. The single-line JSON body
  carries exactly ``items`` and ``next_cursor``; each item carries
  exactly ``request_id``, ``status`` and ``created_at`` in ascending
  acceptance order, and ``next_cursor`` is the opaque continuation value
  or ``null`` at the end of the listing. Any other query parameter, a
  duplicated ``status`` value or a malformed filter answers 400.
* ``GET /requests/{request_id}`` -- return the accepted request's
  receipt, scoped to the tenant identified by the ``X-Tenant-Id`` header
  (or a ``tenant_id`` query parameter). The receipt is the record frozen
  at acceptance time and always reports ``accepted``; it never changes
  when the request's status subsequently advances.
* ``GET /requests/{request_id}/status`` -- read-only observation of the
  request's current state. The single-line JSON body carries exactly
  ``request_id``, ``status`` and ``created_at`` in that order; ``status``
  is the latest persisted state while ``created_at`` stays the original
  acceptance time.
* ``GET /requests/{request_id}/execution-log`` -- read-only observation
  of the request's execution attempts. The single-line JSON body carries
  exactly ``request_id`` and ``attempts``; attempts are ordered by
  ``attempt_number`` starting at 1 and each entry carries exactly
  ``attempt_number``, ``claimed_at``, ``lease_expires_at``, ``result``
  and ``completed_at``. An unfinished attempt has ``null`` ``result`` and
  ``completed_at``; a finished attempt carries its stored ``completed``
  or ``failed`` result and completion time.
* ``GET /requests/{request_id}/tombstones`` -- read-only, paginated
  publication of the tenant's deletion proofs for one request. The
  tenant follows the existing ``X-Tenant-Id``/query rule; the only
  query parameters are ``cursor`` and ``limit`` (1..1000, default 100).
  The single-line JSON body carries exactly ``request_id``,
  ``tombstones``, ``recorded_at``, ``evidence_digest`` and
  ``next_cursor`` in that order. ``tombstones`` holds only this page's
  entries in ascending normalized-scope Unicode code point order then
  ascending ``adapter_id``; each entry carries exactly ``adapter_id``,
  ``scope``, ``operation_id``, ``outcome`` (``deleted`` or ``absent``),
  ``proof_digest`` (64 lowercase hex characters) and ``recorded_at``.
  The top-level ``recorded_at`` and ``evidence_digest`` always describe
  the whole ledger (both ``null`` when it is empty), never just the
  page; ``next_cursor`` resumes strictly after this page's last entry
  while the ledger holds a following item and is ``null`` at the end.
  An unknown or duplicated query parameter, an invalid ``limit`` or an
  empty, malformed, foreign or stale ``cursor`` answers 400; an
  invalid, unknown or cross-tenant request id answers 404; a storage
  fault or a corrupt ledger answers 503 and never a partial page or a
  pseudo digest. The read never advances state, never creates an
  attempt or a tombstone and never changes the audit chain.
* ``GET /policy-catalog/versions`` -- read-only publication of the
  tenant's policy-catalog version history, without any subject detail.
  The tenant follows the existing ``X-Tenant-Id``/query rule; the query
  string accepts no parameter other than ``tenant_id`` -- a duplicated
  key, an unknown parameter or an empty or malformed tenant answers 400.
  The body is the verbatim single-line compact UTF-8 JSON text (with its
  single trailing newline) produced by
  :meth:`RequestStore.audit_policy_catalog`: exactly ``versions`` at the
  top level, versions in ascending order, each carrying exactly
  ``version``, ``effective_at``, ``rule_count``, ``exception_count`` and
  ``status`` -- never a policy id, selector, reason, subject or any raw
  catalog content. The read never creates or advances a catalog version,
  request, attempt, tombstone, receipt or audit record, so repeated
  reads and reads after a restart return the same snapshot. A tenant
  without publications answers 200 with an empty ``versions`` array; a
  corrupt catalog or any storage failure answers 503 and never a
  partial history or a fabricated summary.
* ``POST /requests/{request_id}/reconcile`` -- reconcile exactly one
  request's execution record against its persisted state by calling the
  storage layer's :meth:`RequestStore.reconcile_execution`. The endpoint
  takes no business parameters: a missing ``Content-Length`` or a length
  of zero means there is no body; any other body answers 400. On success
  it answers 200 with the same single-line JSON shape as the status
  read -- exactly ``request_id``, ``status`` and ``created_at`` --
  rendering the current record after reconciliation. Repeating the call
  never changes a stable terminal state, historical attempts or existing
  timestamps; concurrent calls leave the unique outcome to the store's
  atomic commit. No subject, scope, idempotency key, worker, lease
  credential or attempt detail is ever exposed.

The observation endpoints never advance state, create an attempt or
write any bookkeeping; they only read persisted rows, so their answers
match the persisted records after a restart. They never expose a lease
credential, worker identity, subject, scope or any other request field.
Only the single-request reconcile endpoint may converge execution state,
through the storage layer's existing atomic semantics; no batch
reconciliation is exposed over HTTP.

Status advancement (:meth:`RequestStore.transition`), the execution
orchestration (:meth:`RequestStore.claim_next`,
:meth:`RequestStore.finish_claim`, :meth:`RequestStore.renew_lease`,
:meth:`RequestStore.transfer_claim`,
:meth:`RequestStore.reconcile_batch`,
:meth:`RequestStore.migrate_execution_leases`) and the deletion receipts
(:meth:`RequestStore.generate_receipt`,
:meth:`RequestStore.verify_receipt`,
:meth:`RequestStore.rotate_receipt_key`) and the anchor capability
(:meth:`RequestStore.verify_chain`,
:meth:`RequestStore.diagnose_chain`,
:meth:`RequestStore.rotate_anchor_key`) and the read-only batched
audit inspection (:meth:`RequestStore.audit_inspection` and
:meth:`RequestStore.audit_inspection_summary`) exist only on
the storage layer and are deliberately not exposed over HTTP: over HTTP
the service opens request acceptance, the acceptance-receipt lookup, the
read-only tenant-scoped listing, the three read-only observation reads,
the single-request execution reconciliation and the read-only
policy-catalog version history described above. The
current-status lookup (:meth:`RequestStore.get_status`), the
tenant-scoped listing (:meth:`RequestStore.list_requests`), the
execution log (:meth:`RequestStore.get_execution_log`), the tombstone
page read (:meth:`RequestStore.page_deletion_tombstones`), the
single-request reconciliation
(:meth:`RequestStore.reconcile_execution`) and the catalog version
history (:meth:`RequestStore.audit_policy_catalog`) back their HTTP
endpoints but remain storage-layer methods as well.

Success responses are a single line of JSON followed by a trailing
newline. Acceptance, receipt lookup, the status read and a successful
reconcile render exactly ``request_id``, ``status`` and ``created_at``
(in that order); the same idempotent request and every lookup return
byte-identical bodies. The execution-log read renders exactly
``request_id`` and ``attempts``. The
listing read renders exactly ``items`` and ``next_cursor``, each item
rendering exactly ``request_id``, ``status`` and ``created_at``. The
tombstone page read renders exactly ``request_id``, ``tombstones``,
``recorded_at``, ``evidence_digest`` and ``next_cursor``, each
tombstone rendering exactly ``adapter_id``, ``scope``, ``operation_id``,
``outcome``, ``proof_digest`` and ``recorded_at``. The policy-catalog
history read renders exactly ``versions``, each version rendering
exactly ``version``, ``effective_at``, ``rule_count``,
``exception_count`` and ``status``.
Error responses are single-line JSON objects with exactly one key,
``error``, holding a stable error code:

``invalid_request`` (400), ``unauthorized`` (401), ``forbidden``
(403), ``idempotency_conflict`` (409), ``not_found`` (404),
``method_not_allowed`` (405) and ``storage_unavailable`` (503).

Optional token authentication and role-based access control can be
enabled by passing an auth configuration (see :func:`load_auth_config`)
to :func:`build_server` / :func:`make_handler`. Without it the service
keeps the unauthenticated contract described above. When enabled every
matched business request must present ``Authorization: Bearer <token>``
for a configured principal: a missing/malformed/unknown token answers
``401 unauthorized`` and a principal lacking the role required by the
endpoint, or acting on a tenant other than its own ``tenant_id``,
answers ``403 forbidden``. ``POST /requests`` requires
``request:submit`` and the target tenant is the body's ``tenant_id``;
each of the five GET endpoints requires ``request:read`` and the target
tenant follows the existing ``X-Tenant-Id``/query rule; the
single-request reconciliation ``POST /requests/{request_id}/reconcile``
requires ``request:reconcile`` and its target tenant follows the same
existing ``X-Tenant-Id``/query rule; the policy-catalog history
``GET /policy-catalog/versions`` requires ``policy:read`` and its
target tenant follows the same existing ``X-Tenant-Id``/query rule.
The configuration keeps accepting the ``request:submit``,
``request:read`` and ``request:reconcile`` roles alone: a principal
without ``policy:read`` simply cannot use the catalog endpoint, and an
existing configuration without it never fails to load. Authentication runs after
path/method routing (unknown paths stay 404, unsupported methods stay
405) but before payload validation and any storage access.
Tokens, roles and the configuration never enter a response, a raised
exception message, a log record, the database or any stored artifact.

No subject, scope, idempotency key, lease credential, worker identity,
database error text, SQL statement or filesystem path is ever placed in
a response, a log record or a raised exception message.
"""
